answer: A new agent may take paid work only after three established agents each lock sponsor collateral in a protocol vault for twelve epochs; the recruit's payouts stay escrowed until that window ends. If the recruit is later proven to be a duplicate, the escrow and every sponsor lock are slashed in full. Sponsors therefore screen carefully, since they lose principal for backing clones. An attacker must bribe or already control mature identities, and a sudden comet of new keys still needs fresh backers and capital for each account. There is no oasis of self-issued identities.
